title: 2017-21 CR-V 1.5T: A/C blows warm, compressor shaft seal leak (seal kit, not a compressor)
summary: Honda Service Bulletin 23-015: oil and refrigerant leaking from the A/C compressor main shaft seal. Inspect the clutch area, hub, and felt washer, sniff the snout, and replace just the shaft seal with the seal kit and special press tool.

specs.name: Labor
specs.value: 1.4 hr seal replacement incl. inspection; 0.7 hr evacuate and recharge

steps.text: Remove the right front tire, undercover, front subframe brace and drive belt.
With the compressor still on the car, look for oil on the clutch area. Oil there means go to the seal repair.
If it's dry, remove the center hub bolt and the hub/armature plate and check both for oil.
If those are dry, pull the felt washer and set it on clean copier paper. Oil transferring to the paper after 10 seconds means go to the repair.
If still nothing, sniff around the compressor snout with a calibrated leak detector for at least 5 minutes. A compressor that hasn't run recently, and a warmer vehicle, give better results.

No leak found: reassemble the hub with its bolt at 17 N·m (13 lb-ft), check pulley-to-armature clearance is 0.30-0.60 mm and shim to suit, reinstall the belt, run 10 minutes and sniff again. Still nothing means check the rest of the A/C system the normal way.
Repair: recover refrigerant, disconnect the hoses and plug the ports right away with the kit's plugs, and remove the compressor.
Remove the clutch (keep the shims, usually 1-2), felt washer, pulley C-ring, pulley and seal C-ring. Clean the bore and shaft with a lint-free cloth, not compressed air.
Pull the old seal with the press and extractor tools from the kit, then clean the bore again and inspect it for damage.

Lube the new seal, seal guide and bore with new POE oil. The seal goes metal side up. Hand-press it about 5 mm below the bore edge, fit the seal C-ring rounded side down, then press to roughly 10 mm until the C-ring snaps into its groove.

Reinstall the pulley with a new C-ring, a new felt washer, the clutch plate with the same shim thickness, and a new hub bolt at 17 N·m (13 lb-ft). Add one can of POE oil to the compressor and reinstall it.

Charge the system, vacuum check, then run MAX COOL for 10 minutes at 1,500-2,000 rpm and sniff the seal area. A leak means replace the seal again; a leak after a second seal means replace the compressor.

body: Related: Honda ServiceNews A21010D (2017-20 CR-V) says to look for insulation fibers on the O-ring section of the hose at the bulkhead before replacing a compressor or discharge hose for a leak. If found, remove the fibers, replace the O-rings and recharge.
